concepts.label: Core file
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the OS-level dump artifact created when a Couchbase Server process panics; 'Couchbase Server honors these core file settings' rather than managing them itself, so this is genuinely OS configuration rather than a Couchbase Server mechanism, and no promoted concept covers it.

notable_absence.finding: This page has zero cross-references to any other page in the corpus - no link to cbcollect_info (which would presumably collect core files as diagnostic information), no link to manage-logging.md (the sibling page for the OTHER main diagnostic artifact, log files), and no link to common-errors.md or troubleshoot.md despite living in the same troubleshoot/ directory as both. It is an entirely self-contained, per-OS configuration checklist (Linux/Ubuntu/RHEL/Mac OS X) with no stated connection to how Couchbase Server actually uses core files once they exist.

cross_component_finding: core-files.md, common-errors.md, and troubleshoot.md are three separate pages in the same troubleshoot/ directory with no links between any of them - each names log files, `cbcollect_info`, or crash artifacts in isolation (this page: core dumps; common-errors.md: log-derived error messages; troubleshoot.md: log files and `cbcollect_info` generally) without ever assembling 'here is everything you should collect together for a Couchbase Support case' into one place. manage-logging.md's own 'Collect Logs' section, which DOES describe `cbcollect_info` in detail, is likewise never linked from any of the three troubleshoot/ pages.
